html:
Rajendra I was king of the Chola Empire from 1014 to 1044 and took it to its greatest size. He was the son of Rajaraja I and shared the throne with him from 1012.

His armies and ships went further than any Indian king's before him:

  • Sri Lanka: in 1017 he finished his father's conquest, captured the Sinhalese king and took the whole island (see Anuradhapura).
  • The Ganges: about 1022 his generals marched 1,600 kilometres north through Odisha and Bengal and beat the Pala king. They brought Ganges water home in pots.
  • Southeast Asia: in 1025 his fleet crossed the Bay of Bengal and raided the ports of Srivijaya in Sumatra and Malaya (see the Chola raid).

To mark the northern march he took the title Gangaikonda Chola, "the Chola who took the Ganges", and built a new capital, Gangaikonda Cholapuram. Its great Shiva temple is modelled on his father's Brihadisvara Temple, and the Ganges water was poured into a huge reservoir beside it.

The raids were about trade as much as glory: Tamil merchant guilds worked the sea route to China. The Chola court sent envoys to the Song emperor in his reign.
